goldens.comment: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.
goldens.reasoning: C2 describes negative offset slicing in OptimizedCursorPaginator raising AssertionError in Django.

goldens.comment: When requests are authenticated with API keys or org auth tokens (which have user_id=None), organization_context.member is None. Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.
goldens.reasoning: C3 identifies member being None causing AttributeError at line 71.

goldens.comment: get_item_key assumes a numeric key, but the paginator is used with order_by=-datetime in the audit logs endpoint; calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime will raise a TypeError.

candidates: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 - Existing paginator now passes negative offsets to the queryset for prev cursors. `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` leaves the offset unclamped for prev cursors. A client-supplied cursor with `is_prev=1` and a negative offset, for example `x:-1:1`, makes `queryset[-1:...]` raise an AssertionError. Before this change the same input also failed, but the change adds a comment claiming it is intended. The `elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra` check still uses the raw offset, which no longer matches the `stop` value. Clamp the offset for all cursors, or validate it in `Cursor`.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:882 - Negative offset slicing on a Django queryset raises an error, and the cursor is user-controlled. With `enable_advanced_features` set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code runs `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start. Django querysets reject negative indexing with `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported.` The comment claiming the ORM handles this is wrong. Any admin can send `optimized_pagination=true` with a cursor like `0:-5:1` and get a 500. If the slice were allowed, it would read rows outside the pagination bounds. Reject or clamp negative offsets, and don't add this path.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 - Privilege check may crash when member is None. `organization_context.member` can be None, for example for a superuser who is not a member of the organization. A non-superuser request would then hit `.has_global_access` on None and raise AttributeError. The expression is also evaluated even when `optimized_pagination` is not requested, so this can break the default path. Compute it only when `use_optimized` is true, and guard against a None member.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:891 - Duplicated paginator code has an inconsistent boundary check. The new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` copies `BasePaginator.get_result` and drops its explanatory comments. For the `is_prev` case it compares `len(results)` against `offset + limit + extra` using the raw offset, not `start_offset`. With a negative offset this never matches, so the extra row is not trimmed and pages come back one item too long. Reuse the base implementation, or use `start_offset` here.
